plan.headline: Across your 16 units, 12 sit below benchmark rents, leaving $29,280 in annual gap that could add $488,000 in equity at a 6% capitalization rate.

actions.title: Address expiring lease renewal for unit 3
actions.why: The lease ends on October 15, 2026 with only 29 days remaining. Current rent of $1,450 sits 14.2% below the HUD benchmark of $1,690. Proposing $1,535 brings a gain if they stay of $1,020 per year, whereas turnover leads to a gain if they leave of -$70 per year.

actions.title: Prioritize vouchers at turnover in 221 E 11th Ave
actions.why: This building has 5 units under benchmark and accounts for $12,240 of your annual gap. Across the portfolio, 9 units are strong candidates for housing vouchers where you have an upside of $29,280 per year. For example, unit 5 has an annual gap of $2,760 below benchmark.

actions.title: Shift renewal end dates toward the seasonal peak
actions.why: Aligning your lease ends with peak months captures $6,581 per year in timing value across your portfolio. Unit A3 ends November 30, 2026, but shifting its cycle to July yields a timing value of $887 per year. Check your state's rules when adjusting lease terms.

skip: Do not push unit A3 to market rent upon departure, because the gain if they leave is -$2,840 per year and requires a payback of 107 months.
Do not aggressively risk turnover in unit 6, where tenant rent burden reaches 54.1% and the gain if they leave is -$1,430 per year.
plan.caution: These projections assume you can capture capped increases of $12,540 per year without exceeding the break-even departure rate of 63.1%.
